The Death of the Traditional OOH Middleman: Will AI Agents Reshape OOH Buying by 2030?

What happens when AI agents can discover inventory, plan campaigns, compare prices, negotiate deals, and optimize performance with minimal human intervention?

Not everyone has the time to read a 35-page magazine, so I wanted to make the key insights more accessible.

Introducing the video version of Media Intelligence -a simple way to explore the ideas, research, and industry perspectives covered in the magazine.

Watch the video, and if something sparks your interest, dive into the full magazine.

Video Download link (10 minutes )- https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a4MM8SP-AbFshIUkZ687E1tanxBEi8kG/view?usp=drivesdk

Full Magazine Link - https://www.linkedin.com/posts/suraj-prakash-8460bb147_the-intelligence-layer-edition-01-2026-suraj-ugcPost-7511315541710675969-gZ7e/

THE DATA BEHIND THE BILLBOARD -EUROPE MARKET DEEP DIVE

Europe’s OOH/DOOH market has a different challenge.

It isn’t simply about growing digital and programmatic OOH. The bigger challenge is connecting multiple national measurement systems, mobility data, audience intelligence, attribution and programmatic infrastructure across different markets.

OOH BRAND LIFT POWERPLAY 2026

From Exposure to Impact: Who Will Own OOH’s Outcome-Intelligence Layer?

OOH has already digitized the screen.

The next challenge is digitizing the intelligence behind the screen.

The industry is moving from:

Delivery → Exposure → Brand Lift → Business Outcome → Optimization

Global OOH reached $54.2B in 2025, with DOOH at $25.5B. Yet programmatic DOOH represented only 7% of global DOOH in the WOO/PwC 2025 benchmark.

THE DATA BEHIND THE BILLBOARD - U.S. MARKET DEEP DIVE

OOH/DOOH is no longer just about screens, locations and impressions.

The real transformation is happening underneath -through mobility data, location intelligence, audience signals, measurement, attribution and optimization.
In my latest research, I explored how the U.S. OOH/DOOH ecosystem is evolving from:

Measurement → Exposure Intelligence → Attribution → Optimization 

I looked at the roles of Geopath, Ipsos, Foursquare, Veraset, Unacast, Precisely/PlaceIQ, Adsquare, Cuebiq, Placer.ai, Comscore and Lumen Research, and how these different data layers connect with planning, DSP/SSP activation and campaign measurement.

The bigger question is not who has the most data?
